scores.evidence: PAN is tokenized before it reaches the scorer. The fraud system sees only token, BIN and last-4
scores.rationale: Correct on inline scoring, in-process GBDT, event-time and watermarks, and tokenization; the "byte for byte" replay and the "0% throughput drop" claims are overstated but minor.

scores.evidence: Sync only for the decision. Everything else is async through Kafka: feature updates, decision logging, case creation, labels, retraining.
scores.rationale: It solves the real inline problem, resolves ambiguities such as issuer vs. processor and the latency budget, and explicitly defers items with triggers.

scores.evidence: One feature definition, streaming first. The same Flink logic writes the online store and is replayed for offline backfill
scores.rationale: The design is consistent with clear ownership; small loose ends include a 30 ms timeout vs. a ≤100 ms budget, and 'strong consistency' for an async decision log.

scores.evidence: Killing the scorer pods causes zero change to auth outcomes, which proves the fallback works.
scores.rationale: Risky latency and fallback assumptions are tested on day one with checkable exit criteria per phase, plus shadow, canary, drift-injection and online/offline mismatch checks and production monitoring.

scores.evidence: The switch gives us ≤100 ms to score. This is the first number to confirm in Phase 0.
scores.rationale: Key assumptions are stated with revisit triggers, but several thresholds (0.5% mismatch, 15% ring fraud, 90-day maturity) are presented without a stated basis.

scores.evidence: Late or duplicate labels handled idempotently (upsert by transaction ID + source)
scores.rationale: It covers fail-open and mass false declines, the fallback chain, bad models, and signed rules and artifacts. Adversarial input, selection bias and dead-letter queues are also covered. Duplicate and reversal handling in the transaction stream and Flink checkpointing are thin.

scores.evidence: GitOps (Argo CD) rolls it out. The switch flag starts at 1%.
scores.rationale: It covers deployment, rollback, alerts, kill switches and approvals, but on-call ownership and incident response are only lightly covered, and the Flink/Kafka/Redis/multi-region burden is heavy for a small team.
Cost is almost absent beyond a build-vs-buy note and 'cost tuning'; there are no cost drivers, scaling or estimates, even though 3× to 5× peak provisioning and active-active are expensive.

Each key decision has an explicit revisit trigger. Vendor and model are isolated (swappable in-process artifact, bought substrate), schemas are versioned and compatibility-checked, and the identity model is treated as foundational.

scores.evidence: Two deployables, split by latency class. ... Nothing finer-grained.
scores.rationale: It is deliberately lean with a long deferral list, but it still has a heavy stack (Flink, Iceberg, multi-region) and some ceremony such as a two-person rule approval.

scores.evidence: Phases (ordered by dependency; within each phase, widest impact first)
scores.rationale: It has a concrete Phase 0 slice, dependency-ordered phases with Unlocks and Depends on, checkable exit checks, and explicit revisit and fallback triggers.

checklist.evidence: a 30 ms hard timeout and a circuit breaker; Online read p99 < 5 ms; CPU inference under 5 ms
If those are also unavailable, approve below a per-MCC amount ceiling and decline above it. Never fail closed globally.
The same Flink logic writes the online store and is replayed for offline backfill, so training and serving cannot drift apart.
Chargebacks arrive 30–120 days late, so labels mature at 90 days.
Dollar-weighted recall at a fixed false-positive ratio (e.g. 1 false positive per 10 frauds), plus decline rate for good customers.
rules are versioned config in git, hot-reloaded and signed, with a per-rule kill switch.
Dispositions show up in the label store within 1 h.
PAN is tokenized before it reaches the scorer. The fraud system sees only token, BIN and last-4
a late/out-of-order policy (watermarks, e.g. 5 s allowed lateness); partitioned by card token
PSI on top features, score distribution, and decline rate by segment; Automatic revert to the last approved model on a performance alarm
The scorer returns {decision, score, reason_codes, rule_version, model_version}
Active-active scoring across 2 regions; Peak load tests at 5× Black Friday traffic.

traps.evidence: Fail to the existing fallback. On timeout or error the switch uses incumbent rules plus network stand-in.
Offline point-in-time joins via replay, so no future data leaks into training.
One definition feeds online and offline; backfill by replay
PAN is tokenized before it reaches the scorer.

note: Strong, risk-first, dependency-ordered plan with a day-one latency and fallback slice and well-handled reversibility. Weak on cost, and it only lightly covers stream duplicate and reversal handling and the explicit p99 budget breakdown.
